findings.label: Saddle nose deformity
findings.evidence: Caption identifies saddle-nose deformity caused by septal cartilage destruction and nasal collapse in a patient with long-term GPA.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Lateral clinical photograph directly demonstrates the captioned GPA-associated saddle-nose deformity. B: Clinical oral photograph shows captioned GPA-associated gingival involvement matching strawberry gingivitis, with additional petechiae and necrosis. C: Clinical photograph and caption identify a specific necrotic tongue lesion in a patient with GPA; no exact vocabulary finding is available. D: Clinical photograph shows hand lesions explicitly captioned as purpura in generalized GPA; the finding is not represented in the allowed vocabulary. E: Clinical photograph demonstrates captioned GPA-associated cutaneous ulceration and necrosis of the left foot.

panels.figure_caption: ENT involvement and skin/mucosal lesions in patients with GPA. (A) Saddle nose deformity (lateral view) in patient with long-term GPA and ENT involvement as a result of septal cartilage destruction with subsequent nasal collapse caused by granulomatous inflammation. (B,C) Mucosal lesions in the oral cavity in two patients with GPA manifesting in one as gingival hyperplasia with petechiae and small foci of necrosis (B) (arrow) and in the other as small necrotic lesions on the tongue (C) (arrow). (D,E) Purpuric lesions on the skin of hands (D) and of the left foot (E) (black arrow) accompanied by ulcerations and necrosis (E) (yellow arrows) in patient with generalised GPA.
in_text_mentions: e most prominent manifestations include nasal crust formation (75%), followed by excessive nose-blowing (70%), nasal obstruction (65%), epistaxis (59%), septal perforation, and saddle-nose deformity (Figure 2A) (27), the latter presenting in 25% of patients as a result of septal cartilage destruction with subsequent nasal collapse, caused by granulomatous inflammation (27). Ear involvement is almost always secondary to nasal involvement and leads to hearing loss, which may be the first GPA symptom. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows gingival hyperplasia with bleeding and friability, compatible with strawberry gingivitis, along with captioned purpura and edema in a child with PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis. B: Panel B is a clinical photograph showing the captioned diffuse erythematous papular rash over the extremities and trunk in a child with PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis. The papular rash is not represented in the allowed findings vocabulary. C: Panel C visibly demonstrates the captioned saddle nose deformity and scattered purpura in a child with PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Eye masking is present but does not prevent classification of the panel.

panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced chest CT from a patient with definitively established GPA demonstrates a thick-walled cavitary pulmonary nodule with irregular margins, a characteristic manifestation. A red arrow highlights the lesion.
panels.attribution_text: Wang et al. Beyond Infection and Malignancy: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Pulmonary Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.101192. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 8.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest showing a cavitary nodule with irregular margins, corresponding to necrotizing granulomatous inflammation confirmed on histopathology. CT: computed tomography
in_text_mentions: At follow-up in August 2008, chest CT showed a marked reduction in the size and number of pulmonary nodules (Figures 7, 8). Pulmonary function testing demonstrated significant improvement, with total lung capacity increasing from 69% to 91% predicted. A definitive diagnosis of GPA was established on the basis of clinical, serologic, radiologic, and histopathologic findings.

findings.label: Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation
findings.evidence: Caption: "Histopathology showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with mixed inflammatory infiltrates".

panels.rationale: Single, clear H&E histopathology image from a patient with pulmonary granulomatosis with polyangiitis. The caption specifically identifies necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and geographic necrosis, both characteristic findings of GPA.
panels.attribution_text: Wang et al. Beyond Infection and Malignancy: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Pulmonary Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.101192. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with mixed inflammatory infiltrates and basophilic geographic necrosis (arrow) (hematoxylin and eosin stain). Scale bar: 50 µm
in_text_mentions: CT-guided core needle biopsy demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. Histopathologic examination revealed mixed inflammatory infiltrates with multinucleated giant cells, geographic necrosis, and focal small-vessel vasculitis (Figures 2-4). Special stains and cultures were negative for infectious organisms, and immunohistochemistry was negative for carcinoma.
